newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty tumbles down after Czech crown.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty tumbles down after Czech crown.

text.p: The Polish zloty tumbled to parity rate levels in early Tuesday trade as the continued decline of the Czech crown created a strong currency-buying sentiment on the market, dealers said.

They said that local bank speculation as well as small orders from foreign investors, eager to migrate away from volatile currencies of Central Europe, pushed the zloty down to nearly even with the parity rate.
"Foreign orders on the negative situation surrounding the Czech crown pushed the zloty down," said Tomasz Nowakowski, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. @
But some dealers said that foreign pressure on the zloty was reinforced by speculative zloty sales by Polish banks.
"There doesn't seem to be many foreigners today and speculation could be the engine of the zloty's fall," said Karol Zaluski, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

At 0915 GMT the zloty was at 0.22/0.09 percent above parity, weaker than opening at 0.67/0.29 percent but off morning lows right at the parity rate, which stands at 3.2353 to the dollar and 1.9108 to the mark on Tuesday.
It was at 3.2300/50 to the dollar and at 1.9050/70 to the mark, agains opening's 3.2150/250 and 1.8970/60 respectively.
Dealers said the central had not intervened on the forex market to stop the zloty's fall, but many expect the bank to sell currencies if the zloty fell below the parity rate.
"Much of the market expects the central bank to intervene if the zloty falls below parity," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
Dealers said however that fundementals were much better in Poland than in the Czech Republic, which should create a natural support for the zloty and slowly push it back up. @
"The zloty should return to one percent from parity and then slowly wind its way back up to 2.5 percent as Polish fundementals remain positive," Deutsche's Wozniak said.

The Czech crown fell to minus 10 percent against the mid-point of its former currency basket on Tuesday despite central bank warning that it would defend the local currency from further losses through interventions.
